rootCause: The frontend logout cleared only part of the session. The AuthProvider context and protected store state could remain hydrated, and the HTTP client could still attach an in-memory access token until a reload.
navigationAuthority: AUTH_LOGOUT_EVENT in AuthProvider is the single navigation authority. AuthProvider.logout only awaits finqzAuth.signOut(), while the listener performs setUser(null) and navigate('/login', { replace: true }).
testsExecuted: npm run test -- --run src/auth/finqzAuth.test.ts src/auth/logout-flow.test.tsx src/api/http.test.ts
results: Logout success clears local session state.
Logout network failure still clears local state.
Refresh 400 clears local state, emits auth:error once, and does not loop.
Common route 400 does not clear the global session.
Protected routes redirect to /login after logout.
Requests after logout do not send Authorization.
Refresh 401 clears the session and emits auth:error without retry loops.
Authenticated session hydration continues to work.

tenantEvidence.tenantLocation: Tenant is kept only inside the authenticated user object in src/store/index.ts (user.tenant_id / user.tenantName). There is no separate tenant slice in the store.
tenantEvidence.tenantCleanup: clearLocalAuthState removes user, so tenant data is removed with the session.

residualRisks: Server-side access token revocation remains out of scope for this EPC.
No external protected cache layer was found beyond the frontend store and HTTP auth state.
hmlRevalidationPlan: Validate login, protected navigation, and logout on HML.
Confirm refresh 400/401 returns the user to /login without a redirect loop.
Confirm reload after logout still lands on login because no session remains.
